title: Do You Still Need Duct Cleaning With a UV Light?
h1: Do You Still Need Duct Cleaning If You Have a UV Light?
description: A UV light keeps your AC coil cleaner, but it doesn't remove dust or debris from ducts. Here's what each one does and when your ducts need cleaning.
quick_answer: Yes, sometimes. A UV light in your HVAC system targets mold and bacteria growing on the coil and drain pan, where the lamp shines directly. It doesn't remove dust, pet hair, construction debris or rodent mess from the ducts. If your ducts are dirty, a UV light won't clean them. The two do different jobs and often work well together.
body:
A UV light and duct cleaning solve different problems, so having one doesn't replace the other. The UV lamp keeps living growth in check on the parts it can see, mainly the evaporator coil and drain pan. Duct cleaning physically removes the dust and debris that builds up inside the duct runs. If that debris is there, light won't make it go away.

What does a UV light in the HVAC system actually do?

Most residential UV lights are UV-C lamps mounted inside the air handler or furnace cabinet, aimed at the indoor coil. The coil gets cold and wet every time the AC runs, which makes it a natural place for mold and bacteria to grow. Constant UV exposure keeps that growth from taking hold.

That helps in a few ways:

  • A cleaner coil moves heat better, so the system doesn't work as hard
  • Less growth means fewer musty smells when the AC kicks on
  • The drain pan is less likely to grow slime that clogs the condensate line

Some lamps are mounted in the supply or return duct to treat moving air. Those have a harder job, because air moves past the lamp in a fraction of a second.

What can't a UV light do for your ducts?

UV light only works on surfaces it shines on directly. Ducts bend, branch and run across the attic, so nearly all of the duct interior is in the dark. And UV has no effect on non-living debris. It won't touch:

  • Dust and fine dirt that has settled along the duct walls
  • Drywall dust and sawdust from a remodel
  • Pet hair and lint built up in returns
  • Droppings or nesting material from rodents that got into the ducts
  • Smoke residue after a wildfire season

A UV light also does nothing for leaks. If a return duct in the attic is torn or disconnected, it keeps pulling attic dust into the system no matter how many lamps you install.

When do you still need duct cleaning?

We don't recommend cleaning ducts on a fixed schedule just because time has passed. It makes sense when there's a reason, such as:

  • You can see dust or debris inside the ducts or blowing out of registers
  • You've just finished a remodel or had drywall work done
  • Rodents or insects have been in the ductwork
  • You moved into a home and don't know the system's history
  • There's visible mold inside the ducts, after the moisture cause is fixed
  • Smoke got into the house and the smell keeps coming back when the system runs

Our air duct cleaning crews put the system under negative pressure, agitate debris loose and pull it out through a sealed collection unit, so it isn't blown around your house.

Should you do both?

In a lot of homes, the best order is to clean the ducts first, then add a UV light to keep the coil clean going forward. Starting with a clean system means the lamp is protecting a clean coil instead of trying to keep up with years of buildup.

That combination is especially useful near the coast, where the marine layer keeps things damp, and in homes where someone has allergies or asthma. A good filter rounds it out. The filter catches particles, the UV handles growth on the coil, and periodic cleaning deals with whatever gets past both.

What maintenance does a UV light need?

UV-C lamps fade over time even when they still glow, so they need replacing on the manufacturer's schedule, often about once a year. Dust on the bulb also cuts its output, so the lamp should be wiped clean during routine service.

Never look directly at a UV-C lamp, and don't open the cabinet to check it while it's on. Most units have a safety switch that shuts the lamp off when the panel comes off. If yours doesn't, ask a technician to look at it during your next tune-up.
faqs: Does a UV light keep ducts clean?
Not really. It keeps the coil and drain pan cleaner by stopping mold and bacteria where the lamp shines. It doesn't remove dust or debris from the ducts, most of which never see the light.
How often should ducts be cleaned if I have a UV light?

There's no fixed schedule. Clean them when there's a reason, such as visible debris, a remodel, rodent activity or smoke contamination. The UV light doesn't change that much, though it can keep musty smells down between cleanings.
Can UV lights damage my HVAC system?

UV-C can break down some plastics and rubber over time, so lamps should be positioned so they don't hit drain pans, wiring insulation or flex duct directly. A professional install takes that into account.
